name: Priya Raman

five_sec.what_is_it: eMeals, which I already use. The home page is a video and a slogan.
five_sec.who_for: Families who want a weekly plan chosen for them.
five_sec.trust_why: The service works for me, but the page shows nothing concrete: no price, no diets, no renewal terms.
five_sec.next_step: Check the plan list for vegetarian and the cost question.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: I know it sends a list to Walmart; the first screen itself does not say either way.

full_page.what_stopped_me: 15 plans and none called Vegetarian, only Plant Based, which drops the eggs my children eat. Price is still hidden in the FAQ; I know it is $59.99 a year and it renewed without warning once.
full_page.whats_missing: A vegetarian plan, a way to share the plan with my mother-in-law, and renewal terms on the page.

EM.quote: Fifteen meal plans, Keto and Paleo included, and still no Vegetarian. 'Plant Based' is not the same thing in my house.

five_sec.what_is_it: An AI meal planner for families.
five_sec.who_for: Families who want planning done automatically.
five_sec.trust_why: Polished, 90,000+ families, but no diet options or price visible, and the main button is a CEO letter.
five_sec.next_step: Look for diet settings and pricing.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Menu screens on a phone; it is an app.

full_page.what_stopped_me: $25 a month is $300 a year, five times eMeals. Messages are metered. The page never says vegetarian.
full_page.whats_missing: Diet filters and a yearly price.

OL.quote: The family group chat is exactly what my mother-in-law needs, but not at $25 a month plus $0.30 per extra message.

five_sec.what_is_it: A dinner planner that texts the whole household the options, then fills a Walmart or Instacart cart.
five_sec.who_for: Households where more than one adult needs to see the plan. That is my situation.
five_sec.trust_why: Honest statements up front ('We don't deliver food', 'no card'), but no ratings or reviews, and I do not see diet options on the first screen.
five_sec.next_step: Check vegetarian and the renewal terms.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: The bold line under the description: 'We don't deliver food.'

full_page.what_stopped_me: The sample week has chicken tenders and meatballs, and the diet tabs are kid-friendly, under 20 minutes, under $75 and gluten-free. Vegetarian appears only in an FAQ list on the pricing page. It looks like an afterthought.
full_page.whats_missing: A vegetarian sample week, and confirmation that profiles handle 'no meat, eggs OK'.

DD.quote: $39 a year, no card for the trial, an email three days before billing, and my mother-in-law gets the plan by text. If only the sample week weren't chicken.

five_sec.what_is_it: Meal-kit delivery behind a 'reveal your offer' pop-up.
five_sec.trust_why: A gamified offer before any information.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: Boxes of ingredients are the product.

full_page.what_stopped_me: There is a Veggie plan, but prices sit behind a zip code and the fine print confirms auto-renewal and shipping on every later box.
full_page.whats_missing: A price, and any honesty about renewal outside the fine print.

HF.quote: 'Offer only valid for new customers with qualifying auto-renewing subscription purchase.' I have been surprised by one renewal already.

five_sec.what_is_it: Recipe organizer, planner and grocery list.
five_sec.who_for: People who cook from their own recipes.
five_sec.trust_why: Ratings on both stores and 'no card required' on the first screen.
five_sec.next_step: Read the pricing page and renewal terms.
five_sec.delivers_food_why: It is clearly an app for recipes and lists.

full_page.what_stopped_me: I would be doing all the planning myself on a pharmacy break, and the Walmart connection is only a vague 'grocery delivery' line.
full_page.whats_missing: Suggested meals and a named Walmart one-tap cart.

PTE.quote: 'No surprise renewals: we don't auto-bill when your year ends unless you choose to.' Best line I read today. My own dal recipes would fit, too.

dd_offer.why: The pricing card, the note under it and the FAQ all agree: 14 days of Family, no card, add a card to keep it, email three days before.
dd_offer.expect_day_15: Family texting stops and I am on the free plan. I am charged nothing unless I chose to add a card.

head_to_head.reason: It does what eMeals does for less, shares the plan with my mother-in-law, and the renewal terms are honest. Vegetarian is the open question.

EM.reason: $39 versus $59.99 a year, household texting, and renewal stated plainly.

PTE.reason: Narrowly: DinnerDrop plans the week and fills Walmart; Plan to Eat has better renewal terms but leaves the planning to me.

OL.reason: Same household-sharing idea at a fraction of the price.

HF.reason: Groceries I choose versus an auto-renewing box.

dd_fix_that_would_move_me: Home page 'See a week' section: add a Vegetarian tab with a real vegetarian week (eggs allowed), and list the diets DinnerDrop supports near the top.
